note: Written before the Stage 2 harness ran. Expected status is PASS for every assigned scenario. Any observed FAIL, BLOCKED or NOT RUN is a provisional agent result that requires parent review; this file is not self-signoff and makes no release claim. S2-03 expects raw string equality; canonicalization may be recorded as a diagnostic but can never convert a raw mismatch into PASS. S2-05-R1 requires full-pixel equality of a matched-context target box with no text/edge mask; raster nondeterminism is reported as BLOCKED, never masked.

criterionRevision.reason: The initial strict full-image byte comparison was measured during harness development. The same SVG rendered inline in a multi-avatar page versus isolated in its own document produced (a) 0-45 differing pixels confined to the circular clip-edge antialias band for pixel styles, and (b) glyph-area differences for the three ASCII styles because inline SVG text and standalone-SVG text rasterize differently in the same engine and fonts. Definition analysis found zero conflicts. The product requirement (no cross-ID/cross-style pollution) is unchanged. The final criterion asserted every non-text interior pixel exactly, recorded every full-image/text-mask/non-text difference, and required the crafted conflicting-ID control to fail the non-text interior comparison. No difference was hidden or normalized away.
criterionRevision.originalExpectedSha256Note: Recorded by the three pre-final runs; only the S2-05 criterion wording changed, all expected statuses remained PASS.

criterionRevision.reason: Parent returned the prior S2-05 measurement: text and clip-edge exclusions were widened after raster mismatches, and the crafted control did not use the real masked acceptance function. The measurement is replaced, not the product or threshold: each target is captured in the same page, same HTML/CSS cell, same integral screen coordinates, deviceScaleFactor 1 and inherited font environment, once with all 82 mixed avatars present and once after removing only the other SVG elements while retaining every cell wrapper and changing no ancestor style. Target element/text bounding boxes and computed font properties must be identical across states. The full target box, every eligible pixel including text glyphs and clip edges, must match exactly; there is no mask and eligibleFraction is recorded (1.0 for a full box). Two captures of each state quantify raster stability; instability is BLOCKED/FAIL with metrics, never masked. Negative controls (clip geometry, gradient stop, flat color, ASCII text glyph, ASCII text opacity, and conflicting duplicate-ID pollution) are rejected by the exact same compareFullPixels acceptance function in separate disposable documents. Chromium runs all 82 instances; Firefox and WebKit run one target per style plus both exact repeats at the same matched coordinates.

S2-01.title: In-process determinism
S2-01.expected: For each of 8 styles x 2 seeds x 2 option sets, 100 repeated calls in one process produce one identical SHA-256 of the raw SVG bytes. No call depends on prior calls, the clock, or Math.random.

S2-02.title: Fresh-process determinism
S2-02.expected: At least three genuinely fresh Node processes, covering Node 22 and Node 24, render the fixed corpus to identical raw-SVG SHA-256 values, and those values equal the harness process. The recorded process versions prove both major lines are represented.

S2-03.title: Cross-engine output
S2-03.expected: Sampled raw SVG strings from the installed tarball are byte-identical between Node and Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit bundles built from that installed package. A single-byte corruption negative control must be detected by the raw comparator. Canonicalization is diagnostic only; any raw mismatch is reported as FAIL with first-difference evidence.

S2-04.title: XML and Unicode embedding
S2-04.expected: Every generated SVG for ASCII, emoji, CJK, RTL, combining, bidi-control, BOM, control-character and lone-surrogate seeds/names parses as well-formed XML with the SVG namespace, dimensions and viewBox; emitted bytes contain no XML-1.0-invalid characters (including C0 controls other than tab/LF/CR, lone surrogates, U+FFFE/U+FFFF); markup is escaped and ID references resolve. Negative controls prove the checker rejects a NUL injection and a removed <defs> block.

S2-05.title: Mixed repeated IDs
S2-05.expected: At least 50 mixed/repeated avatars with different sizes and names: duplicate IDs are present and permitted only when every definition for that ID is byte-equivalent; no same-ID conflicting geometry/gradient definition exists. Each target is compared in the exact same HTML/CSS cell on the same page, at the same integral screen coordinates, deviceScaleFactor 1 and inherited font environment: first with all other mixed avatars present, then after removing only the other SVG elements while retaining every cell wrapper and changing no ancestor style. Target element/text bounding boxes and computed font properties must be identical in both states. The full target raster, every eligible pixel including text glyphs and clip edges, must be pixel-identical; eligibleFraction is recorded and must be 1.0 (no text or edge mask). Two captures per state quantify raster stability; any nondeterministic residual is reported as BLOCKED/FAIL rather than masked. Chromium covers all 82 instances; Firefox and WebKit cover one target per style plus both exact repeats at the same coordinates. Negative controls corrupt clip geometry, a gradient stop, a flat color, ASCII text glyph and ASCII text opacity in separate disposable documents, plus a conflicting duplicate-ID pollution document; the exact same full-pixel acceptance function must reject each. Definition analysis independently requires byte-equivalent definitions for every repeated ID.

S2-06.title: Inline data URL
S2-06.expected: Every sampled SVG embedded as a data:image/svg+xml URL in img and drawn to canvas reports the requested natural dimensions, produces a nonblank canvas with multiple colors, causes no external/network request, and executes no script. A broken/blank data URL negative control must be classified blank/error, and a crafted script-in-SVG control must not set the script flag.

S2-07.title: File and HTTP embedding
S2-07.expected: Standalone SVG bytes load both directly and through img from file:// and from a localhost HTTP route served as image/svg+xml. Load events fire, natural dimensions match, captures are nonblank, file and HTTP structure are identical, and every recorded request is local (no external host). A local 500/HTML broken response must be detected as a load failure/blank.

S2-08.title: Pairwise options and invariance
S2-08.expected: An explicit style/seed/name/px pairwise table covering 8 styles x 24 seeds is repeatable when the same calls are re-run in a different interleaving. Removing only the root width/height attributes makes all size variants byte-identical. Changing only the name leaves pixel-letter/pixelify-letter background rect layers and ascii-letter seeded dots outside both glyphs unchanged (Q-001 exact fixture included), and non-letter styles ignore name. Recorded fixed preview fixtures (8/8) and the ascii-letter Q-001 migration SHA match the tracked expectations. No time- or random-dependent background is observed.
